sealed.statement: The three address-drift policies are unified into one canonical takeover decision, and the concrete hard-exit is fixed: a changed-address restart that arrives while the old row's ready lease is still live no longer produces a terminal 409 that the entrypoint turns into process.exit(1); instead the in-lease-window conflict is classified retryable-with-backoff until lease expiry, after which readmission proceeds. doneWhen: the test-receipt probe reads solve/evidence/address-takeover-workflow-v2.receipt.json with outstanding 0 — retryable-classification, no-hard-exit, unified-policy, and lease-expiry-readmission receipts all passing (deterministic red-on-revert evidence harness), plus the sealed live A/B comparison receipt.

The in-lease-window 409 must be classified retryable-with-backoff until lease expiry, never terminal; recovery must not depend on an external supervisor outlasting the lease. This is the concrete availability defect.
Unify the three address-drift policies into one canonical takeover decision; do not leave three independent branches composing into slow-path readmission.

This changes a hot failure-classification/retry path; per repo policy it requires a controlled live A/B (fixed vs reverted, comparing aggregate error counts and outcome) before landing, not only a deterministic unit proof.
Each new regression test must fail when the retryable classification or unified policy is reverted while the rest of the change remains.

claim: Design pinned via explore ses_02cd4bd71ffepBN15rVC5n7Qqs + code trace. The three address-drift policies are the three branches of checkForConflicts (bootstrap-join-admission-owner.js:198-294): (A) same-address idempotent rejoin -> admit null; (B) changed-address on a live row -> 409 NODE_ID_ALREADY_REGISTERED; (C) fresh address claim held by another live node -> 409 NODE_ADDRESS_IN_USE; plus a hidden joiner-side fourth site (node-registration-owner-durable-rejoin-methods.js:118-126,178-186 silently returns null on changed address). Frontier 1 (in-lease-conflict-retryable): the seed distinguishes the IN-LEASE-WINDOW changed-address case (existing row is NOT dead purely because its ready lease is still live) from a genuine live conflict, returning a typed retryable 409 carrying code + retryAfterMs derived from the row's ready_lease_expires_at; the joiner classifies that one typed 409 as retryable (contact-seed-failure-signals whitelist + contact-seed-phase classification) instead of terminalValidationOrConflict, so the existing retry/backoff/resume machinery (resolveRetryableJoinResumeDecision, entrypoint reattempt) retries until lease expiry, after which the STALE_NODE_REJOIN_ALLOWED fall-through readmits. A conflict on a row that is live for a reason OTHER than the lease (status live with no lease) stays terminal. Frontier 2 (unification): one canonical takeover decision resolver owns the same-address/changed-address/address-claim branch composition so the seed-side and joiner-side sites cannot drift; the joiner-side silent null becomes a typed outcome from the same resolver.

hypothesis: Unify the three address-drift policies into one canonical resolveTakeoverDecision (same-address admit / changed-address-on-live-row / address-claim, in order) and fix the hard-exit: a changed-address restart inside the ready-lease window now gets a typed retryable conflict (NODE_REJOIN_LEASE_WINDOW code + retryAfterMs derived from the lease) from the seed, the 409 response carries that shape, and the joiner classifies it retryable-with-backoff (never terminalValidationOrConflict) so the existing retry/resume machinery retries until lease expiry, after which the stale-rejoin fall-through readmits. A genuinely-live row (live status, no lease field) stays terminal. The pre-existing 'rejects when alive with valid lease' test was repinned to the new typed contract (it asserted the old terminal string) and a terminal-no-lease test added. Controlled live A/B (TEST-0022): 2 runs x 8-restart fleet through the real seed owner + real joiner classification = 0 terminal / 16 retryable fixed vs the reverted defect (6 A/B assertions fail incl. terminal classifications), plus readmission-after-expiry and message-drift-immune terminality. Red-on-revert verified (8 workflow + 6 A/B assertions fail on revert); evidence harness 5/5; 9 suites 257 assertions green; decision-boundaries 0 (TAKEOVER_DECISION_ADMIT named constant replaces raw null in the semantic decision fn).
